'''Mark Daniel Reckase''' is an [[educational psychologist]] and expert on [[Quantitative psychology|quantitative methods and measurement]]<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Mark Reckase|url=https://touchstoneinstitute.ca/people/mark-reckase/|access-date=2021-04-26|website=Touchstone Institute|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=2021-03-27|title=Reckase, Mark|url=https://us.sagepub.com/en-us/nam/author/mark-d-reckase|access-date=2021-03-30|website=SAGE Publications Inc|language=en}}</ref> who is known for his work on [[computerized adaptive testing]],<ref>{{Cite news|last=Gewertz|first=Catherine|date=2011-05-16|title=Computer-Adaptive Testing Poses Challenges, Expert Warns|url=https://www.edweek.org/leadership/computer-adaptive-testing-poses-challenges-expert-warns/2011/05|access-date=2021-04-26|website=Education Week|language=en}}</ref> multidimensional [[item response theory]], and [[Standard-setting study|standard setting]] in educational and psychological tests.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Do Educational Assessments Yield Achievement Measurements, Mark D. Reckase, Michigan State University|url=https://www.ets.org/s/research/videos/36617_angoff-lecture-2017_transcript.html|access-date=2021-04-26|website=www.ets.org}}</ref> Reckase is University Distinguished Professor Emeritus in the College of Education at [[Michigan State University]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Update on VP election {{!}} IACAT|url=http://www.iacat.org/update-vp-election|access-date=2021-03-30|website=www.iacat.org}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
2016: Career Award from the [[National Council on Measurement in Education|National Council for Measurement in Education]] for Contributions to Educational Measurement.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Awards - NCME|url=https://www.ncme.org/awards/2016-awards|access-date=2021-03-30|website=www.ncme.org|language=en}}</ref>

2009: Michigan State University Distinguished Professor<ref>{{Cite web|title=MSU faculty earn University Distinguished Professor title|url=https://msutoday.msu.edu/news/2009/msu-faculty-earn-university-distinguished-professor-title|access-date=2021-03-30|website=MSUToday {{!}} Michigan State University|language=en}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Reckase graduated from the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign|University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]] in 1966 with a B.S. in psychology. He earned his Ph.D. in psychology from [[Syracuse University]] in 1972, where his advisor was [[Eric F. Gardner]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Reckase|first=Mark|date=1972-01-01|title=Development and Application of a Multivariate Logistic Latent Trait Model|url=https://surface.syr.edu/psy_etd/126|journal=Psychology - Dissertations}}</ref> His dissertation was titled ''Development and application of a multivariate logistic latent trait model.''

Reckase began his career on the faculty at [[University of Missouri]] in 1972. In 1981, he moved on to a position as Assistant Vice President for Assessment Innovations at [[ACT, Inc.|ACT]]. In 1998, he left ACT to join the faculty of the College of Education at Michigan State University. He retired in 2015.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Reckase wins top career award in educational measurement - News - The Latest at the College of Education – Michigan State University|url=https://education.msu.edu/news/2016/reckase-wins-top-career-award-in-educational-measurement/|access-date=2021-04-23|website=education.msu.edu|date=7 April 2016 }}</ref>

Between December 2001 and November 2006, Reckase was chief editor of the academic journal ''[[Applied Psychological Measurement]]''.<ref>{{cite journal |author1-link=David J. Weiss |last1=Weiss |first1=David J. |title=New Apm Editor Now Accepting New Manuscript Submissions |journal=Applied Psychological Measurement |date=December 2001 |volume=25 |issue=4 |pages=315–316 |doi=10.1177/01466210122032154|s2cid=121179508 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1-link=Mark L. Davison |last1=Davison |first1=Mark L. |title=New Editor's Statement: Continuity and Change |journal=Applied Psychological Measurement |date=January 2007 |volume=31 |issue=1 |page=3 |doi=10.1177/0146621606295551|doi-access=free }}</ref> He has served as President of the International Association for Computerized Adaptive Testing (2017)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Keynotes {{!}} IACAT|url=http://iacat.org/node/2469|access-date=2021-04-26|website=iacat.org}}</ref> and as President of the National Council on Measurement in Education (2008-2009).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Board of Directors - NCME|url=https://www.ncme.org/about/board/past-presidents|access-date=2021-04-26|website=www.ncme.org|language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==
Reckase specializes in the development of educational and psychological assessments, particularly the [[Psychometrics|psychometric]] theories underpinning the development of such tests.<ref name=":2" /> He has worked extensively in multidimensional item response theory since the beginning of his academic career: his dissertation was on the early development of a multidimensional [[Item response theory|item response model]] and he went on to write a book on the topic in 2009.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Reckase|first=Mark|title=Multidimensional item response theory|date=2009|publisher=Springer|isbn=978-0-387-89976-3|location=New York|oclc=437345698}}</ref> He has branched out into other psychometric areas, like standard setting.<ref>{{Cite book|last=RECKASE|first=MARK|title=THEORY OF STANDARD SETTING.|date=2020|publisher=CHAPMAN & HALL CRC|isbn=978-1-4987-2211-7|location=[Place of publication not identified]|oclc=1048445795}}</ref>

== Representative publications ==
*Reckase, M. (1979). Unifactor latent trait models applied to multifactor tests: Results and implications. ''Journal of Educational Statistics, 4'', 207–230.
*Reckase, M. (1985). The difficulty of test items that measure more than one ability. ''Applied Psychological Measurement, 9'', 401–412.
*Reckase, M. (1997). The past and future of multidimensional item response theory. ''Applied Psychological Measurement, 21'', 25–36.
*Reckase, M. (2006). A conceptual framework for a psychometric theory for standard setting with examples of its use for evaluating the functioning of two standard setting methods. ''Educational Measurement: Issues and Practice, 25'', 4–18.
*Reckase, M. D., & McKinley, R. L. (1991). The discriminating power of items that measure more than one dimension. ''Applied Psychological Measurement'', ''15''(4), 361–373.
